== 1.9.13 | 2026-11-15
- If the owner dismisses your request to turn the server on, the launcher now says so (Request denied), and you can ask again.
- New names: the program on the server machine is Gatehouse Keeper, and its window there is the control panel. In the launcher, the Remote host panel tab is now Remote control panel, and Helper control is Keeper control.
== 1.9.12 | 2026-11-15
- Nothing you'll notice: each device now keeps its list of places to fetch updates from in step with the pack, so the pack's address on GitHub can change without setting devices up again.
== 1.9.11 | 2026-11-15
- The launcher and its tools are now called Gatehouse. The window's title bar reads Gatehouse, and the pack's settings in the game's mod menu are now Gatehouse Settings (same switches, same place). The pack, the server and your shortcuts are still October Journey.
== 1.9.10 | 2026-11-15
- Nothing you'll notice: the launcher and the update now take the pack's name and details from a settings file shipped with the pack instead of having them built in. Groundwork for using the same launcher with more than one server.
== 1.9.9 | 2026-11-15
- Fixed: the server showed a red dot while online when the server panel no longer accepted this device's saved sign-in. The dot now follows the server (green when online), and the Control line says the sign-in is no longer accepted and to sign in again under Server config; Start and Stop are greyed out until then.
== 1.9.8 | 2026-11-15
- For devices the owner has allowed Helper control, Manage launchers is now the Remote host panel tab, with two tabs inside: Manage access (who may do what, by launcher or by player with all their devices) and Host activity (whether MCSS and the Minecraft server are running, and what was asked of the server machine).
== 1.9.7 | 2026-11-15
- When the server is off, the Play button becomes Request server: it asks the owner's PC to turn the server on (it chimes there and shows who asked). The button turns back into Play by itself when the server is online. One request a minute.
- The first two tabs are now Client updates and Server updates.
- Restart is yellow and Quit is red.
== 1.9.6 | 2026-11-15
- Server controls: the first section is now Server Machine, with Wake server machine and Sleep server machine.
- Server config is now just the server panel sign-in (username, password, Sign in, Sign out), right in the tab. Open server panel and the Server access window (API key, internet wake address) are gone.
- Manage launchers is a tab of its own, for devices the owner has allowed Helper control.
- A device now controls the server in one of two ways: through the host helper (the owner allows it) or with your server panel sign-in. Keys issued by the owner are gone; a key already saved on a device keeps working.
== 1.9.5 | 2026-11-15
- Play is blue when it's ready, and only works while the server is online; until then it's greyed out and lights up by itself when the server comes up (start it under Server controls if you're allowed).
- When an update asks before downloading, the Play button becomes Download and accepts it. Skip this time is gone: Download continues, Quit cancels the launch.
== 1.9.4 | 2026-11-15
- The question before an update downloads now also says where it downloads from: the owner's PC over Tailscale or GitHub for the pack's own files, and Modrinth for mods.
- The launcher tells the server PC which Minecraft account last played on this device (the name only), so the owner can manage access per player. It counts once you've joined the server from the device.
== 1.9.3 | 2026-11-15
- Quit in the launcher can now cancel a launch without Prism treating it as a failure and opening its log. It needs a small launch wrapper set up for the instance: new installs get it, and the owner switches it on for existing devices.
== 1.9.2 | 2026-11-15
- Fixed on Windows: "The update didn't finish" when an update brought a new launcher. Windows wouldn't let the update replace the launcher while its window was open; the launcher now runs from a copy. If you saw that message, press Restart once (or launch again).
== 1.9.1 | 2026-11-15
- The launcher says how this device controls the server (Server controls and Server config): through the host helper, with an API key the owner issued, with your panel sign-in, or with an API key entered here.
- The owner can issue your device its own server key from the server PC: the launcher picks it up by itself, nothing to type or paste.
- The owner can see how each device controls the server and remove it. Your device then forgets any sign-in or key it had saved.
- MCSS control now includes starting and stopping the Minecraft server.
- Clearer message when the server PC's own access to MCSS is the problem.
== 1.9.0 | 2026-11-15
- Before an update downloads, the launcher says about how big it is (and how many mods and files) and asks: Download, Skip this time (play with what's installed; the server may not accept it) or Quit. With nothing to download it doesn't ask.
- The Server controls and Server config tabs only appear once the owner has allowed your device something in the host panel on the server PC (or you have your own panel access). They come and go as the owner changes it.
- Server control can now be given by the owner: a new Server control permission in the host panel lets your device start and stop the Minecraft server through the server PC, with no panel sign-in or key on your device.
- The launcher updates itself first: when an update brings a new launcher, it fetches that before anything else and reopens straight away, so launcher changes show on the same launch (from the update after this one).
- Manage launchers (Server config): for a device the owner has allowed Helper control, a window like the host panel on the server PC, to see the launchers, switch their Server control, MCSS control and PC sleep, and forget one. Helper control itself is only given on the server PC.
== 1.8.9 | 2026-11-15
- Server controls are grouped in three sections: Server PC (wake, sleep), MCSS (start, close) and Minecraft server (status, ping, players, start, stop), each with its own status line.
== 1.8.8 | 2026-11-15
- Sleep server PC (Server controls): puts the server PC to sleep, for devices the owner has allowed (a separate permission from MCSS control), and only while the Minecraft server is stopped. Wake server device wakes it again from the home network.
== 1.8.7 | 2026-11-15
- Fixed: with MCSS closed, the launcher said the server PC was asleep. It now says the PC is awake but MCSS isn't running (and Wake stays greyed out).
== 1.8.6 | 2026-11-15
- Server controls show your ping to the server as ten pips from red to green (more is better), with the number of players connected below it. Both come straight from the game server, no panel access needed.
- Start server can only be pressed while the server is off, Stop server only while it's running, and Wake server device only while the server PC isn't answering.
- The Server tab starts with a live line (online with ping and players, off, or not answering), since the rest of the tab is the server as last recorded.
== 1.8.5 | 2026-11-15
- Server controls and Server config scroll when their content is taller than the window, and long messages wrap instead of being cut off.
- The MCSS close button says what it will do: Close MCSS when MCSS's X button exits it (a normal close), Force close MCSS when its X button only hides it (MCSS is ended). Either way only once the Minecraft server is stopped.
== 1.8.4 | 2026-11-15
- Fixed: Server controls said MCSS wasn't running when it was (so Close MCSS stayed greyed out).
== 1.8.3 | 2026-11-15
- Server controls can start and close MCSS (the server software) on the server PC: Start MCSS and Close MCSS. Each device asks once and the owner allows it in the host panel on that PC. MCSS only closes once the Minecraft server is stopped.
== 1.8.2 | 2026-11-15
- Server controls have a tab of their own, and a Stop server button beside Start (it asks first, since it disconnects anyone playing; the world is saved).
- After Stop, the tab watches the shutdown and says whether it went smoothly: the server stopped and its log shows the world being saved.
- Open server panel and Server access moved to a new Server config tab, which also shows whether this device has panel access.
== 1.8.1 | 2026-11-15
- Nothing starts the game by itself any more: no countdowns. The window waits until you press Play, and closing it is the same as Quit.
== 1.8.0 | 2026-11-15
- One window from the moment you press Play: a checklist of the update's steps, ticked off as each finishes (with the download's progress), which then becomes the summary. No more windows flashing up during the update.
- Beside Play: Restart runs the update again, and Quit cancels the launch.
- Server access can sign you in with your server panel username and password, so there's no API key to copy. The password isn't saved.
== 1.7.4 | 2026-11-15
- Server access has Paste buttons beside the API key and wake address (the Steam Deck's on-screen keyboard can't paste), and a Show box to check the key.
== 1.7.3 | 2026-11-15
- The Server tab shows whether the server is online (and how many players are on, with a server panel key), and has buttons to wake the server's PC, start the server, and open the server panel in your browser.
- Wake server device works from the home network. Start server needs an API key from the server panel: add it once under Server access; it's kept on your device only.
== 1.7.2 | 2026-11-15
- The pop-up has a Server tab: what the server runs (game version, Jarvis, mods, settings) and what changed there since you last played. When something's new on the server, the button reads Next: server changes and takes you there before the game starts.
== 1.7.1 | 2026-11-15
- The pack's settings mod is now called October Journey Settings (Mods > October Journey Settings): it has the mod switches and the pop-up switches.
- Devices set up before the pack hid Inventory Profiles Next's purple Auto Refill arrows on the hotbar now get that default once. Turn them back on in that mod's settings if you like them.
- The program that installs the pack's updates now stays on a fixed version, so it only changes when the pack does.
- The update before each launch copes better with a bad connection: if the network isn't up yet it waits and tries again, a download that fails or stalls is tried again from the other source, a stalled one is stopped after 5 minutes, and it never stops to show its own error window.
- Steam's overlay notifications no longer cover the pop-up's Play button.
- The pop-up now lists everything the update checked, with a coloured dot for how each went, and the mods it added, removed or updated.
== 1.7.0 | 2026-11-14
- New Steam shortcut, October Journey: it updates the pack, starts the game and joins the server in one go. To add it, close Steam, run the setup again and pick Add the October Journey shortcut.
- The Prism Launcher shortcut now shows Prism Launcher's own logo, and both shortcuts get the Steam Deck controller layout.
- Running the setup again keeps your mod switches and pop-up settings.
== 1.6.0 | 2026-11-14
- A pop-up like this one now shows before the game starts: what's new after an update, or that you're up to date (that one closes itself after 5 seconds).
- Turn either pop-up off in Mods > October Journey (Update pop-up, No-update pop-up).
== 1.5.0 | 2026-11-14
- Every mod that isn't a library can now be switched off in Mods > October Journey. All are on by default, except the two nearby-chest mods.
- New installs hide Inventory Profiles Next's Auto Refill arrows on the hotbar (change it in that mod's settings).
== 1.4.0 | 2026-11-14
- Stack to Nearby Chests and Nearby Chest Crafting are off by default. Switch them on in Mods > October Journey.
== 1.3.6 | 2026-11-14
- Fixed the first launch on a new install sometimes starting without the pack's mods.
== 1.3.5 | 2026-11-14
- If the mods can't be installed on the first launch, it stops and asks you to press Play again instead of starting plain Minecraft.
== 1.3.4 | 2026-11-14
- Setup and the uninstaller offer a quick install or a choice of each part, and where it goes.
== 1.3.3 | 2026-11-14
- Chat moves up to fit Steam's keyboard on any screen size.
== 1.3.2 | 2026-11-14
- With a Steam controller, Steam + X opens Steam's keyboard and chat moves up above it.
== 1.3.1 | 2026-11-14
- Typing with Steam's keyboard works while using a Steam controller.
== 1.3.0 | 2026-11-14
- Steam controllers use Steam's keyboard; other controllers keep Controlify's own keyboard.
== 1.2.2 | 2026-11-14
- The update that runs before each launch keeps itself up to date.
== 1.2.1 | 2026-11-14
- The October Journey server stays in your multiplayer list with the right address.
== 1.2.0 | 2026-11-14
- Steam library art and the Steam Deck controller layout are kept up to date.
== 1.1.0 | 2026-11-14
- Controller support (Controlify) on every device, with fixes for Steam controllers and the Steam Deck.
== 1.0.0 | 2026-11-14
- The first October Journey pack.
